scope:
Repair the negative-control probe classifier in scripts/shiki_github.py so `shiki secret set-claude` works against the current Claude CLI.

ROOT CAUSE, MEASURED 2026-08-20. `_classify_probe_result` decided PROBE_AUTH_REJECTED solely by regex-matching the CLI's prose against `_AUTH_REJECTION_MARKERS`, whose first entry is commented "the negative control's real signature" and was seeded from `401 Invalid bearer token`. The current CLI returns `Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid.`. The list carries "invalid token"; the actual phrase is "access token is invalid" — the same words reversed — so `_AUTH_REJECTION_RE.search(...)` returns None and the payload falls through to PROBE_INDETERMINATE. `verify_claude_oauth_token` requires the negative control to be PROBE_AUTH_REJECTED, so it returned "could not prove token-exclusive verification" for EVERY candidate token, valid or not, and `cmd_secret_set_claude` refused to set the secret.

FIX. The probe payload already carries a structured field the classifier ignored: `api_error_status`. Add `_AUTH_REJECTION_STATUSES = frozenset({401, 403})` and `_auth_rejection_status(result)`, which accepts the int or digit-string form and returns None for absent / boolean / non-numeric / non-auth statuses. Consult it in `_classify_probe_result` BEFORE the success branch, so a payload carrying an auth status is never PROBE_AUTHENTICATED whatever `is_error`, `subtype` or `total_cost_usd` claim — the CLI reports `subtype: "success"` even on this failure, so neither field is load-bearing. Keep the wordlist as the fallback for CLIs that report no status and add "token is invalid" for the reversed word order.

DELIBERATE OMISSION, stated so it is not "helpfully" re-added. Do NOT add "oauth access token" as a marker. It is a topic noun, not a rejection predicate: a non-auth failure such as "Connection error while refreshing OAuth access token" would then read as a clean rejection, and the negative control would certify a token-exclusivity it never proved. That WEAKENS the fail-closed posture this module exists to hold. "access token is invalid" is already covered by "token is invalid", and `api_error_status` covers the rest. A test pins that string as INDETERMINATE.

FAIL-CLOSED IS UNCHANGED. A genuinely indeterminate probe — network error, CLI crash, non-JSON, rate limit, 5xx — must still classify as PROBE_INDETERMINATE and still refuse to set the secret.

DOCS. docs/agents/runtime-auth-model.md states the negative control's expected rejection as "(e.g. `401 Invalid bearer token`)". That example encodes the very assumption that broke; de-pin it and state the structured-status-first rule.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py && for s in scripts/test_shiki_*.sh; do bash "$s" || exit 1; done
title: Classify probe auth rejections from api_error_status, not CLI prose
